intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Deadly high-speed train crash in Spain
items.text: Two high-speed trains collided near Toledo in central Spain, and at least 68 people have died. Nearly 100 others were injured, according to reports. First aerial pictures of the wreckage were released on Wednesday, showing the scene of the crash. Ten South Korean passengers were reportedly on board, and two of them suffered minor injuries. Investigators have not yet said what caused the collision, and the number of victims could still change.

gloss.collide: to hit another moving thing with great force
gloss.wreckage: the broken parts left after a crash
gloss.aerial: seen or taken from above, for example from a plane or drone
gloss.on board: travelling in a vehicle such as a train or plane
gloss.investigator: a person whose job is to find out what happened

items.title: India evacuates thousands as cyclone hits
items.text: India has moved tens of thousands of people to safety as Cyclone Arnab made landfall on Wednesday. A cyclone is a powerful storm with strong winds and heavy rain, and it can damage homes and flood roads. Officials ordered people in the most exposed areas to leave before the storm arrived. Emergency teams are now checking the damage along the coast.

gloss.evacuate: to move people away from a dangerous place
gloss.make landfall: to reach land after moving over the sea
gloss.cyclone: a powerful storm with strong winds that turns in a circle
gloss.exposed: not protected from bad weather or danger
gloss.flood: to cover dry land with water

items.title: Healey's first Budget hits landlords and banks
items.text: Chancellor John Healey delivered his first Autumn Budget on Wednesday. Tax on property and savings income will rise by 2p from next April, taking the rates to 24p, 44p and 49p. The surcharge on bank profits goes up by three percentage points for 15 months, and the plan to cut the cash ISA limit has been dropped. The government says borrowing will fall to 1.8% of national income by 2030. Growth is forecast at 1% next year, down from 1.6%.

gloss.chancellor: the government minister in charge of taxes and public money
gloss.surcharge: an extra tax added on top of the normal one
gloss.drop: to decide not to go ahead with a plan
gloss.borrowing: money a government takes from lenders to pay for its spending
gloss.forecast: to say what you expect to happen in the future

items.title: Liverpool and City win League Cup shoot-outs
items.text: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties at Anfield after a 1-1 draw in the League Cup fourth round. Morgan Rogers scored for Chelsea from the spot, and Cody Gakpo equalised for Liverpool, also from the penalty spot. Manchester City then won a shoot-out against Brighton after a 2-2 draw at the Etihad. Fleetwood, a fourth-tier club, had knocked out Arsenal on penalties on Tuesday. Liverpool will now face Bournemouth in the quarter-finals.

gloss.shoot-out: a way to decide a drawn match, with players taking turns to shoot from the penalty spot
gloss.equalise: to score a goal that makes the score level
gloss.knock out: to remove a team or player from a competition
gloss.quarter-final: a match with eight teams left, before the semi-finals

items.title: Djokovic through in Basel, Ruud beaten
items.text: Novak Djokovic, who is playing in Basel on a wildcard, beat Ugo Humbert 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in the round of 32. In the last 16, Nuno Borges upset ninth seed Casper Ruud 1-6, 6-3, 6-4 to reach the quarter-finals. Holger Rune also went through after a tiebreak in the deciding set against Hubert Hurkacz. The Swiss Indoors runs until 1 November.

gloss.wildcard: a place in a tournament given to a player without the usual qualifying
gloss.upset: to beat a player who was expected to win
gloss.seed: a player ranked highly and placed in the draw to avoid early meetings with other top players
gloss.tiebreak: a short game used to decide a set at 6-6
gloss.go through: to win and move on to the next round

items.title: OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google chips
items.text: OpenAI plans to buy artificial intelligence chips from Google, according to a report on Wednesday. The chips are Google's Tensor Processing Units, known as TPUs. OpenAI already rents them, and it uses a large number of Nvidia chips as well. A direct purchase would help it depend less on one supplier. The financial terms and the number of chips have not been made public, and neither company has confirmed a deal.

gloss.supplier: a company that provides goods or services to another
gloss.rent: to pay to use something for a time
gloss.terms: the conditions and details of an agreement
gloss.confirm: to say officially that something is true

items.title: Sauna session boosts immune cells, study finds
items.text: A Finnish study has found that one sauna session can raise the number of white blood cells in the body. Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland studied 51 adults with an average age of 50. Each person spent 30 minutes in a sauna, with a short cold shower halfway through. Every type of white blood cell rose, but counts were back to normal within 30 minutes. The scientists say the study does not show lasting health benefits.

gloss.white blood cell: a cell in the blood that helps the body fight infection
gloss.participant: a person who takes part in a study

items.title: Jay-Z to headline 2027 Super Bowl show
items.text: The NFL has confirmed that Jay-Z will headline the halftime show at the 2027 Super Bowl. The rapper and the league announced the deal on Tuesday, after days of speculation. Halftime performances are watched by one of the biggest television audiences of the year. Many fans had doubted that the announcement would happen so soon. Further details of the show have not been published yet.

gloss.headline: to be the main performer at an event
gloss.halftime: the break in the middle of a match
gloss.speculation: guesses about something without clear facts
gloss.audience: the people who watch or listen to something
gloss.announcement: a public statement about something new

items.title: Samsung profit passes 100 trillion won
items.text: Samsung Electronics has reported third-quarter operating profit of more than 107 trillion won, about $80 billion. It is the first Korean company to pass 100 trillion won in a single quarter. Profit rose almost ninefold from a year earlier, driven by memory chips and demand for AI computing. Samsung will pay a total cash dividend of 30 trillion won. Weak smartphone sales may dampen the results of its devices division.

gloss.operating profit: money a company makes from its main business, before some costs and taxes
gloss.quarter: a period of three months in a company's financial year
gloss.dividend: a share of profit paid to the people who own shares
gloss.dampen: to make something weaker or less strong

items.title: GTA VI reviews expected on 18 November
items.text: Rockstar Games has reportedly started sending review copies of Grand Theft Auto VI to journalists. Insider NateTheHate said first reviews are expected on 18 November, two days before the game's release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Some players had feared a last-minute delay, but this news has eased those worries. Rockstar has also turned some real places in Miami into Vice City themed locations as part of its marketing. Rockstar has not confirmed the review date.

gloss.insider: a person with private knowledge of a company's plans
gloss.review copy: a free copy of a game sent to journalists before release
gloss.ease: to make a worry or problem smaller
gloss.last-minute: happening very close to the deadline
gloss.themed: designed to look like a particular idea or place
